en: to be dangerous; to be risky; to be unsafe

examples.en: It's dangerous here, so go play over there.
It's dangerous to run next to the water.

examples.ko: 운전 중에 휴대폰을 보는 건 정말 위험하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think looking at your phone while driving is really dangerous.
This building is old and looks dangerous.

explain: 반대는 '안전하다'예요. 명사 '위험'과 함께 '위험이 있다'처럼도 써요. 급할 때는 '위험해!'라고 짧게 외치기도 해요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날은 위험한 길이 많아요.
phrases.en: There are many dangerous roads on rainy days.
phrases.nuance_en: '위험한' modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: This ride is not dangerous.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not dangerous.

phrases.en: It's dangerous to go alone at night.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form.

explain_en: Plain, general word for danger (위험한 길) Its opposite is '안전하다' (safe). It also works with the noun '위험', as in '위험이 있다'. In an emergency people shout just '위험해!'.

en: to be strange; to be weird

examples.en: This milk tastes weird.
That friend is a bit strange today.
At first it was strange, but now it's fine.
The computer is making a strange noise.
Strangely, I'm not hungry today.
Isn't it weird? I put it here. But it's gone.

explain: '이상하다'는 보통과 달라서 이해가 안 되거나 불안한 느낌이에요. '신기하다'는 놀랍고 흥미롭다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. '이상하게'는 '왜 그런지 모르게'라는 느낌으로 자주 써요. 숫자 뒤의 '이상'(以上)은 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I hear a strange sound at night.
phrases.nuance_en: '이상한' modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: Strangely, I'm sleepy today.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feeling of 'for some reason'.

phrases.example: 그 옷은 이상하지 않아요. 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: Those clothes aren't weird. They suit you well.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not strange.

explain_en: General everyday word for anything odd or not right. '이상하다' describes something different from normal that feels puzzling or unsettling. '신기하다' carries a positive sense of wonder and interest. '이상하게' is often used for 'for some unknown reason'. The '이상' (以上, 'or more') after numbers is a different word that just sounds the same.

dis.h: general; odd, off, or not right

p.n: 묘하다 means the taste is odd in an intriguing, hard-to-describe way; 이상하다 means something is off.

examples.ko: 가족과 함께 있을 때 제일 행복해요.
examples.en: I'm happiest when I'm with my family.

examples.ko: 우리 네 식구는 행복하게 살고 있어요.
examples.en: Our family of four lives happily.
Are you happy these days?
Have a happy day!
I feel happy when I see a healthy child.
I was really happy today.

explain: '기쁘다'는 어떤 일에 대한 순간의 감정이고 '행복하다'는 삶이 전체적으로 만족스러운 상태를 말해요. '즐겁다'는 하는 일이 재미있을 때 써요. 반대는 '불행하다'이고, '행복해지다'로 변화를 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My family wants to live happily.
phrases.nuance_en: '행복하게' modifies the verb.

phrases.en: I become happy when I meet my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행복하지 않던 상태에서 변하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes changing into a happy state.

phrases.en: I'm not very happy these days.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are not happy.

explain_en: General personal feeling of happiness or contentment; everyday (저는 행복해요). '기쁘다' is a momentary feeling about an event, while '행복하다' describes a state where life feels satisfying overall. '즐겁다' is for when an activity is enjoyable. The opposite is '불행하다', and '행복해지다' expresses becoming happy.

gh: auspicious; a joyful occasion or event

p.n: 단란하다 stresses a close, harmonious family rather than a general feeling.

usage: 가장 = most (written/formal). 제일 = most (common in speech).

examples.en: This shop's cake is the most delicious.
This building is the tallest in Seoul.
I'm the youngest at my company.
Today is the coldest day this week.
The hospital is the closest one around here.

explain: ‘가장’과 ‘제일’은 뜻이 같아요. 말할 때는 ‘제일’을 더 많이 쓰고, ‘가장’은 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. ‘N 중에서 가장’, ‘N에서 가장’처럼 비교하는 범위와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I like summer the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘가장’과 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 가장, but more common in speech.

phrases.en: What is your favorite food?
phrases.nuance_en: '가장 좋아하는 + noun' is a common way to say 'favorite'.

phrases.en: I study Korean the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양이나 횟수가 제일 많을 때 ‘가장 많이’라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the amount or number is the highest.

dict_examples.ko: 그 아이가 우리 반에서 가장 빠르다.
dict_examples.en: That kid is the fastest in our class.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Grandfather loved my older brother the most.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The biggest cause of obesity is overeating.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 요즘 이 책이 가장 잘 팔린다.
dict_examples.en: This book is the best seller these days.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Neutral to formal; works in speech and writing (가장 맛있다). ‘가장’ and ‘제일’ mean the same thing. In speech ‘제일’ is more common, while ‘가장’ shows up more in writing and the news. Use it with the range you're comparing, as in ‘N 중에서 가장’ or ‘N에서 가장’.

p.n: 제일 is more everyday; 가장 is slightly more formal.

t90.ax: I'm the youngest at my company.

examples.en: That employee's explanation was too hard to follow.
My friend's directions are very detailed.
This word is hard to explain.
The staff member's explanation of the menu is kind and clear.
Is my explanation difficult? — No, it's easy.

explain: ‘설명해 주세요’처럼 ‘-아/어 주다’와 같이 자주 써요. 잘못한 일의 이유를 말할 때 ‘설명’은 중립적이지만, ‘변명’은 핑계를 대는 느낌이라서 ‘변명하지 마세요’처럼 나쁘게 들려요.

phrases.en: The teacher explains the grammar.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해요 to 설명 makes it a verb.

phrases.en: Please explain this word.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with -아/어 주세요 to make a request.

phrases.en: I need a detailed explanation.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 자세한 when the explanation is detailed.

dict_examples.ko: 새 기획안에 대한 설명이 끝나자 질문이 쏟아졌다.
dict_examples.en: As soon as the explanation of the new proposal ended, questions poured in.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 친구의 설명만으로는 문제가 이해되지 않아서 선생님께 질문하기로 했다.
dict_examples.en: My friend's explanation alone didn't help me understand the problem, so I decided to ask the teacher.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 아무런 설명도 없이 갑자기 집으로 갔다.
dict_examples.en: He suddenly went home without any explanation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 설계도에는 상세한 도면과 설명이 덧붙여져 있었다.
dict_examples.en: Detailed drawings and explanations were attached to the blueprint.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: General word for making something clear. It's often used with ‘-아/어 주다’, as in ‘설명해 주세요’ (Please explain). When giving reasons for a mistake, ‘설명’ is neutral, but ‘변명’ sounds like making excuses, as in ‘변명하지 마세요’ (Don't make excuses).

t90.ax: This word is hard to explain.

examples.en: I work out in the park in the evening.
I don't exercise these days.

examples.ko: 무슨 운동을 좋아해요? — 저는 수영을 좋아해요.
examples.en: What sports do you like? — I like swimming.
I exercise twice a week with a friend.
Let's have lunch together after the workout.

explain: ‘무슨 운동 해요?’라고 물으면 ‘축구’, ‘수영’, ‘요가’처럼 운동 이름으로 대답해요. 헬스장에서 기구로 하는 운동은 보통 ‘헬스’라고 해요. ‘환경 운동’, ‘독립운동’의 ‘운동’은 사회를 바꾸려는 활동(movement)이라는 다른 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: I exercise in the park every morning.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter way to say 운동을 해요.

phrases.en: My friend likes exercise very much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아하는 것을 말할 때 ‘을/를 좋아해요’를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 을/를 좋아해요 to say what you like.

phrases.en: The children play on the playground.
phrases.nuance_en: The big open area for sports at a school.

dict_examples.ko: 적당한 운동은 건강에 좋으나 지나친 운동은 해가 될 수도 있다.
dict_examples.en: Moderate exercise is good for your health, but too much can be harmful.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 매일 운동으로 다져진 다리는 나이답지 않게 단단했다.
dict_examples.en: Toned by daily exercise, his legs were firm beyond his years.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: If someone asks ‘무슨 운동 해요?’, answer with the name of a sport, like soccer, swimming or yoga. Working out with machines at the gym is usually called ‘헬스’. In ‘환경 운동’ (environmental movement) and ‘독립운동’ (independence movement), ‘운동’ means a social movement — a different sense.

examples.ko: 저 다리를 건너면 바로 학교가 나와요.
examples.en: If you cross that bridge, the school is right there.
The bridges over the Han River are really beautiful at night.

examples.ko: 새로 생긴 다리 위에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took photos on the newly built bridge.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 다리 위로는 차가 못 가요.
examples.en: Because of construction, cars can't go onto the bridge.
This bridge is fifty years old.
The river flows slowly under the bridge.

explain: '다리'는 몸의 다리와 소리와 글자가 같아서, '건너다'나 '한강 다리'처럼 함께 쓰는 말을 보고 구별해요. 다리는 보통 '건너다'와 함께 쓰고, 다리를 만드는 것은 '놓다'를 써요. 큰 다리 이름에는 '한강대교'처럼 '-대교'도 많이 붙어요.

phrases.example: 저 큰 다리를 건너면 시장이 바로 나와요.
phrases.en: If you cross that big bridge, the market is right there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 가다가 강이나 도로 위의 다리를 지나갈 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing over a bridge above a river or road while traveling.

explain_en: Everyday word for a bridge; also means leg of a body. '다리' is spelled and pronounced the same as the word for a body leg, so you tell them apart from words it goes with, like '건너다' or '한강 다리'. A bridge is usually something you '건너다' (cross), and building one is '놓다'. Names of big bridges often end in '-대교', like '한강대교'.

t90.ax: This bridge is fifty years old.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 따뜻한 만둣국이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On cold days I want to eat warm dumpling soup.
If you stir an egg into the dumpling soup, it gets softer.
One bowl of dumpling soup here, please.

examples.ko: 만둣국은 만두가 커서 한 그릇이면 배불러요.
examples.en: The dumplings in this soup are big, so one bowl fills you up.
I took care of dinner simply with dumpling soup.

explain: 만두를 넣고 끓인 국이에요. 글자는 'ㅅ'이 있지만 '만둗꾹'처럼 발음해서 'ㄱ'이 된소리로 나요. 떡을 넣으면 '떡국', 둘 다 넣으면 '떡만둣국'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I boiled dumpling soup and ate it on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_en: Soups use '끓이다' for making them.

phrases.en: I like rice cake and dumpling soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떡과 만두를 둘 다 넣은 국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soup with both rice cakes and dumplings.

phrases.en: One bowl of dumpling soup, please.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

explain_en: It is a soup boiled with dumplings. The spelling has 'ㅅ' but you pronounce it '만둗꾹', with 'ㄱ' turning tense. With rice cakes it is '떡국', and with both it is '떡만둣국'.

examples.ko: 신입생은 학교생활을 알기 위해서 선배에게 질문해요.
examples.en: New students ask seniors questions to learn about school life.

examples.ko: 학부모 상담 때 담임에게 아이의 학교생활을 자세히 물어봤어요.
examples.en: At the parent meeting I asked the homeroom teacher in detail about my child's school life.
School life is fun, but there is a lot of homework.
At my new school, school life still feels unfamiliar.
Once I made friends, school life became enjoyable.

explain: 학교에 다니면서 겪는 수업, 친구, 행사 같은 전체 생활을 말해요. '학교생활을 하다'보다 '학교생활이 재미있다/힘들다', '학교생활에 적응하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 대학교에서는 '대학 생활'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: School life is fun these days.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how you feel about school.

phrases.en: My younger sibling adjusted well to school life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 학교에 익숙해질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when getting used to a new school.

phrases.en: How is college life?
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에 다니는 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for life while attending university.

explain_en: It covers everything about attending school: classes, friends and events. People more often say '학교생활이 재미있다/힘들다' or '학교생활에 적응하다' than '학교생활을 하다'. For university, '대학 생활' is the common phrase.

examples.ko: 저는 내일 시험이 있어서 도서관에서 시험공부를 해요.
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I'm studying for it at the library.

examples.ko: 시험공부를 할 때 단원마다 핵심어를 따로 적어 두면 편해요.
examples.en: When studying for a test, it's handy to note key words for each unit.

examples.ko: 시험공부는 도서관에서 하는 게 집중이 잘돼요.
examples.en: Studying for exams at the library helps me concentrate.
I'm not getting enough sleep because of exam study.
When you study for a test, keep your phone far away.
I turned off my phone to focus on studying for the test.

examples.ko: 시험공부가 끝나면 영화를 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: When I'm done studying for the exam, I'll go see a movie.

explain: 시험을 위해 하는 공부를 말해요. 시험 전날 한꺼번에 몰아서 하는 것은 '벼락치기'라고 하는데, 영어의 cramming에 더 가까운 말이에요. '시험공부를 하다'가 가장 자연스럽고, 가까운 말로 '시험 준비'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Is your exam preparation going well?
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부뿐 아니라 시험을 위한 모든 준비를 말해서 조금 더 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than studying; covers all preparation for an exam.

phrases.example: 시험공부 때문에 요즘 잠을 못 자요.
phrases.en: Because of studying for exams, I can't sleep these days.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying for the test is the reason.

phrases.en: I study for the exam together with my friend in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람과 함께 공부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying together with someone.
phrases.en_equiv: to study for a test together

explain_en: It means study done for a test. Doing it all at once the night before is called '벼락치기', which is closer to English 'cramming'. '시험공부를 하다' is the most natural phrase, and a related expression is '시험 준비'.
